intent: Should I expand my coffee business into Japan?

tasks.subQuestion: How large and fast-growing is Japan's coffee market?

findings.title: Japan Coffee Market Report 2025
findings.content: Japan is the world's fourth-largest coffee importing country, consuming roughly 430,000 tonnes per year. Specialty coffee sales grew about 6% annually from 2020 to 2024, while canned and convenience-store coffee volumes were flat.

findings.title: Specialty coffee boom in Tokyo
findings.content: Independent third-wave cafes in Tokyo increased by an estimated 30% since 2019. Operators cite high rents in central wards as the main constraint on expansion.

findings.title: Japan cafe chains ranked by store count
findings.content: Starbucks Japan operates about 1,900 stores, Doutor roughly 1,300 and Komeda around 1,000. Convenience stores sell over 1 billion cups of fresh-brewed coffee annually at around 100-150 yen per cup.

tasks.subQuestion: What are the import rules and entry costs?

findings.title: Importing food products into Japan: a guide
findings.content: Roasted coffee imports require notification under the Food Sanitation Act. Green coffee beans enter duty-free; roasted coffee carries a tariff of up to 12% depending on origin and trade agreements. Opening a 30-seat cafe in Tokyo typically costs 15-30 million yen.

intent: Is it a good time to invest in electric vehicle stocks?

findings.title: Global EV sales outlook
findings.content: Global EV sales rose about 25% year over year, but growth in the US slowed to single digits as incentives changed. China accounts for roughly 60% of global EV sales.

findings.title: EV sector valuations after the selloff
findings.content: The EV sector trades at a median forward P/E of 38 versus 19 for the broader auto industry. Several EV startups have less than 12 months of cash runway.

findings.title: Analysts split on EV makers
findings.content: Analysts are divided: bulls point to falling battery costs, bears to price wars in China squeezing margins.

intent: Where can I buy my father a nice suit and tie?

tasks.subQuestion: Which menswear stores in New York sell quality suits?

findings.title: The best menswear shops in Manhattan
findings.content: Madison Avenue and SoHo host most of Manhattan's tailored menswear. Mid-range ready-to-wear suits start around $600; made-to-measure typically runs $1,200-$2,500 with 4-6 week turnaround.

tasks.subQuestion: Where can suits be altered quickly?

findings.title: Fast suit alterations in NYC
findings.content: Many Midtown tailors offer 48-hour alterations for hemming and sleeve adjustments, typically $40-$120.
